summary: 400 China Basin is a 148-unit, 100% affordable homeownership condominium development (8 stories; sources give different building areas, see open questions) in Mission Bay South, developed by China Basin Partners LLC (Curtis Development, Michael Simmons Property Development and Young Community Developers), designed by Mithun with associate architect YA Studio, and built by general contractor Nibbi Construction/Baines Group; it held a ribbon-cutting on September 26, 2025 (Office of the Mayor release of that date; the project's press release had announced the date and SF YIMBY reported on October 2 that it had taken place the week before).

milestones.text: OCII releases the RFP for Mission Bay South Block 9A seeking an affordable-homeownership development team
MSPDI/Curtis Development/YCD's sole proposal received by the July 22, 2019 deadline, scored 90.6/100 (the exact submission day is not stated)
OCII Loan Committee approves $3.5M in predevelopment financing
OCII Commission approves the project's Basic Concept and Schematic Design
OCII Loan Committee approves $71,684,522 in permanent gap/predevelopment financing
Construction reported 50% complete, on budget, about three weeks delayed by winter rain

OCII staff memo (dated this day) asks the Citywide Affordable Housing Loan Committee for an additional $8,000,000 in gap funding, which would bring total OCII investment to $83,184,522, to offset rising mortgage rates' effect on affordability; no approval date is shown in the sources read

Ribbon-cutting held (Office of the Mayor release of this date: the Mayor "today cut the ribbon"; the developer's August 2025 press release had announced the date and SF YIMBY reported on October 2 that it had been held the week before)

costs.what: OCII (public) investment/loan as proposed in the Oct 2023 staff memo: the $75,184,522 considered in Nov 2021 plus a requested additional $8M (approval not shown in the memo); the developer's 2025 press release gives "$83 million from the City through OCII"
State of California Infill Infrastructure Grant (IIG)

facts.value: 400 China Basin St (Mission Bay South Block 9A)
China Basin Partners LLC ('350 China Basin Partners, LLC' in some OCII filings), joint venture of Curtis Development, Michael Simmons Property Development, Young Community Developers
Mithun (architect of record), with associate architect YA Studio and landscape architect GLS
Nibbi Construction and Baines Group (named together as the general contractor)
148 (100% of units are below-market-rate affordable homeownership)
Sale prices restricted to households earning 80-110% AMI, individual units priced at 75/85/95/105% of AMI; average affordability target about 90% AMI
Sources differ (180,063 or about 200,000 sq ft); lot is 29,939 sq ft (0.69 acres) per OCII
~85 (zoning allowed up to 90 for the block)
100% affordable, permanently price-restricted homeownership condominiums (OCII Limited Equity Program)
State of California Infill Infrastructure Grant funding, OCII permanent/gap financing (forgivable loan), homebuyer sales proceeds, and a private construction loan from Goldman Sachs
Type I (concrete) construction, U-shaped 8-story building over a podium; foundation uses roughly 200-ft driven piles due to Bay Mud fill conditions
Targeted GreenPoint Rating 195 in 2021 planning (RFP minimum 125); GreenPoint Rated Platinum per the project's press release; all-electric with solar panels per SF YIMBY
~34 spaces (0.23-0.25 cars/unit), unbundled from unit sales

open_questions: Square footage is inconsistent across sources: 180,063 sq ft (OCII 2021 filing) vs. ~200,000 sq ft (SF YIMBY 2025) vs. 165,000 sq ft (the architect's own page) -- possibly different measurement conventions, not resolved.

Total development cost is not shown because the figures differ. OCII's November 5, 2021 Evaluation of Request for Financing gives \"Total Development Cost (TDC): $134,220,472\" and \"TDC/unit: $906,895\" on its project-description page, and a sources-and-uses total of $135,145,636 ($913,146 per unit) on page 5 (both pre-construction estimates); the developer's August 21, 2025 press release calls it a \"$130 million project\"; no final as-built figure was found in a post-completion OCII/MOHCD document.
OCII's Oct 2023 memo projected a temporary certificate of occupancy in August 2024, roughly 13 months before the Sept/Oct 2025 opening; no source explains the gap.

The general contractor's name appears variously as 'Nibbi Construction,' 'Nibbi Brothers' and 'Baines-Nibbi JV' across OCII documents; the OCII evaluation lists the contractor as 'Nibbi | Baines' in its project table and 'Nibbi Construction/Baines' in a later table, and its section 5 says 'selecting a JV of Baines-Nibbi JV'; the two firms are treated as one pairing, and the architect's news post names only 'Nibbi'.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

When construction began: OCII's loan memo of 2023-10-20 (Loan Committee, 400 China Basin additional gap funding) says "Project financing closed in June 2022, and construction began in July 2022" (Section on financing); SF YIMBY (2025-10-02) says "Construction had started for the eight-story multiunit complex in 2023". The sources disagree by a year, so this record shows no construction-start milestone. The OCII memo, written after the event, also reports construction 50% complete as of September 1, 2023, which is the earliest construction date shown here.
Building area: OCII's 2021 filing gives 180,063 sq ft of total building area (129,712 residential); SF YIMBY's 2025 completion article cites approximately 200,000.
